en: To praise enthusiastically and publicly; public praise
hook: AC-CLAIM: everyone CLAIMS it's great — loudly.
story: Acclaim. Enthusiastic public praise; as a verb, to praise publicly. Rehana, a young director from Bogura, shot her first film in her grandmother's village with local actors and almost no money. She sent it to an international festival without much hope. At the premiere, the audience rose and clapped for ten long minutes, and Rehana [gasp] covered her face with both hands. Critics around the world acclaimed it. Acclaim comes from the Latin for shouting toward, the same root as clamour: acclaim is praise you can hear. So, what word means loud, public praise? ... Acclaim.

gre.s: Although her early novels were ignored, her final book won universal ____, earning every major literary prize that year.
gre.clue: earning every major literary prize that year

example: The young cricketer from Sylhet was acclaimed across the country after scoring a century in his very first test match.

en: Very skilled or proficient at something
hook: ADEPT: an ADEPT is an ADEPT-ed expert.
story: Adept. Very skilled at something. Nobody in Rashed's family could fix anything electrical, except his twelve-year-old niece, Mim. With a tiny screwdriver and a few online videos, she repaired the ceiling fan, rewired a frayed charger, and brought her grandfather's old radio back to life. When the radio crackled into a song, her grandfather [laugh] clapped like a boy. Mim was adept at repairs. Do not mix up adept with inept, which sounds similar but means clumsy: adept is its opposite. So, what word describes someone very skilled at a task? ... Adept.

gre.s: Although new to the job, she proved remarkably ____ at calming angry customers, defusing complaints that had defeated her far more experienced colleagues.
gre.clue: defusing complaints that had defeated her far more experienced colleagues

example: My grandmother is so adept at bargaining that vendors at Kawran Bazar lower their prices the moment they see her coming.

en: To learn for sure, usually by checking carefully
hook: AS-CERTAIN: make CERTAIN.
story: Ascertain. To find out for sure, usually by checking carefully. A rumour spread through Nafis's hostel that the Sylhet bus would leave at five in the morning instead of seven. Half the floor rushed to the counter at dawn, yawning in the cold. Nafis did not trust rumours. He called the bus company twice and checked his ticket online to ascertain the real time. It was seven, and he slept two extra hours. Ascertain hides the word certain inside it: to ascertain is to make certain. So, what verb means to find out for certain by checking? ... Ascertain.

gre.s: Before publishing the story, the editor insisted that reporters ____ the facts from at least two independent sources.
gre.clue: from at least two independent sources

example: Before signing the lease, Rumana phoned the previous tenants to ascertain whether the flat really stayed dry during the monsoon.

en: Highly ornate and extravagant in style; excessively complicated
hook: BAROQUE: so ornate it might BREAK under all the decoration.
story: Baroque. Highly ornate and extravagant; also, far too complicated. The wedding stage in the convention hall was astonishing: golden pillars carved with peacocks, crystal chandeliers, thousands of roses, and mirrors on every surface. Not one inch was left plain. Ishrat's grandmother stopped at the entrance, [gasp] then whispered that she did not know where to look first. It was truly baroque. The name comes from the richly decorated style of European churches and music in the seventeenth century, full of golden curls. So, what word describes decoration so ornate that nothing is left plain? ... Baroque.

gre.s: Readers accustomed to the author's spare early style were startled by the ____ prose of her later novels, with their elaborate, ornamented sentences.
gre.clue: with their elaborate, ornamented sentences

example: The tax form was so baroque, with its endless sub-clauses and cross-references, that even the accountant needed a whole afternoon to finish it.

en: Well-meaning and kind; charitable
hook: BENE-VOLENT: wishing (vol) good (bene).
story: Benevolent. Kind and well-meaning; charitable. Every winter, when cold winds sweep across Rangpur, Tahsin's grandfather, a retired schoolteacher, spends part of his pension on blankets. Before dawn, he walks through the poorest lanes of town, handing them out quietly, with no photographs and no speeches. An old rickshaw puller once wrapped himself in one and simply held his hand. The neighbours call him a benevolent man. Bene means good and vol means wish, so a benevolent person wishes others well; its opposite is malevolent. So, what word describes someone kind and generous to others? ... Benevolent.

gre.s: Far from being the ____ patron he appeared to be in public, the landlord privately evicted any tenant who fell even a single week behind on rent.
gre.clue: privately evicted any tenant who fell even a single week behind on rent

example: The mill owner was remembered as a benevolent employer who quietly paid school fees for every worker's children.

en: To support or strengthen
hook: BOLSTER: a BOLSTER is a long pillow that props you up.
story: Bolster. To support or strengthen. Ananya's thesis claimed that the Sundarbans mangroves protect coastal villages from cyclones. Her supervisor frowned. "A big claim needs strong support." So Ananya spent two months gathering storm records, satellite maps, and interviews with fishermen in Satkhira. At her final presentation, nobody could find a weak point. She had bolstered her argument. A bolster is a long, firm pillow that props you up; to bolster a claim is to prop it up with evidence. So, what verb means to support and strengthen? ... Bolster.

gre.s: The prosecutor hoped the new forensic evidence would ____ a case that had, until then, rested almost entirely on a single witness.
gre.clue: rested almost entirely on a single witness

example: A run of easy wins early in the tournament bolstered the young team's confidence before they faced the defending champions.

en: Settling a question completely, leaving no room for doubt
hook: CONCLUSIVE: brings the argument to a CONCLUSION.
story: Conclusive. Settling a question completely, with no room for doubt. For weeks, Sumaiya's hostel floor argued about who was stealing milk from the shared fridge. Everyone had a theory, and friendships began to crack. Then the warden checked the corridor camera, [gasp] and leaned closer. The footage showed a large grey cat nudging the fridge door open every night. The whole floor [laugh] cheered. The video was conclusive. Conclusive comes from conclude: conclusive proof brings an argument to its conclusion. Do not confuse it with conducive, which means helpful. So, what word describes evidence that leaves no doubt? ... Conclusive.

gre.s: Although the early studies were suggestive, they were far from ____, and regulators insisted on a much larger trial before declaring the drug effective.
gre.clue: insisted on a much larger trial before declaring the drug effective

example: DNA testing finally gave conclusive proof that the bones belonged to the explorer who vanished in the Arctic in 1845.

en: Causing or likely to cause argument; quarrelsome
hook: CONTENTIOUS: creates CONTENTION (conflict).
story: Contentious. Likely to cause argument; also, fond of arguing. At Eid lunch, someone mentioned the coming election. Within a minute, uncles were raising their voices, aunties were taking sides, and a cousin had walked out to the balcony. Grandmother tapped her spoon on her glass until the table went quiet. "Not today." Everyone knew politics was the most contentious topic in the family. Contentious comes from contend, to fight or compete: a contentious subject makes people contend. So, what word describes a topic sure to start an argument? ... Contentious.

gre.s: The proposal to build the dam proved highly ____, provoking furious debates in parliament and protests across the region.
gre.clue: provoking furious debates in parliament and protests

example: A plan to cut down the old banyan tree in the village square and pave a parking lot turned contentious within days.

en: The feeling that something is unworthy of respect; to scorn
hook: DIS-DAIN: you won't DEIGN to look at it.
story: Disdain. The feeling that someone or something is not worthy of respect; scorn. At a restaurant in Banani, a man in a gold watch glanced at the plate a young waiter set down, then pushed it away with two fingers, as if it were dirty. The waiter's cheeks burned. At the next table, Nabila felt sick watching. The man's disdain filled the room. Disdain is related to dignity and deign: to disdain something is to treat it as beneath your dignity. So, what word names the cold feeling that someone is beneath your respect? ... Disdain.

gre.s: The aristocrat made no effort to hide his ____ for the newly rich merchants, refusing their invitations and mocking their manners at every opportunity.
gre.clue: mocking their manners at every opportunity

example: The veteran chef spoke of instant noodles with open disdain, though his students often caught him eating them late at night.

en: To break up and move off in many directions
hook: DIS-PERSE: like a SPRAY spreading out.
story: Disperse. To break up and move off in many directions. Thousands of people had gathered at Shahbag for an evening concert when a sudden storm broke. In seconds, the crowd dispersed: under shop awnings, into rickshaws, down every side street. Tanha squeezed into a tiny tea stall with six soaked strangers. Within ten minutes the square was empty, with only a few paper flags left in the rain. Disperse shares a Latin root with sparse, meaning scattered: when a crowd disperses, it scatters. So, what verb means to break up and scatter in all directions? ... Disperse.

gre.s: Once the morning fog began to ____, the hikers could see the trail clearly again, though only an hour earlier the valley had been completely hidden.
gre.clue: the hikers could see the trail clearly again

example: Wind and ocean currents dispersed the oil slick along hundreds of kilometres of coastline within a single week.

en: So firmly fixed that it is very hard to remove
hook: EN-TRENCHED: dug deep into a TRENCH, impossible to move.
story: Entrenched. So firmly fixed that it is very hard to remove. Dowry has been illegal in Bangladesh for decades. Yet in some villages, families still quietly hand over cash, furniture and motorbikes at weddings. When a young teacher named Rokeya refused to let her brother's future in-laws pay one, her own relatives were shocked. The custom is deeply entrenched. Picture soldiers dug into a trench: an entrenched habit is dug in so deep that it will not move. So, what word describes a custom so firmly fixed that it is hard to remove? ... Entrenched.

gre.s: Reformers found it difficult to challenge the ____ bureaucracy, whose habits and privileges had been established over generations.
gre.clue: established over generations

example: The rivalry between the two neighbouring football clubs is so entrenched that grandfathers still argue about a match played in 1975.

en: Not regular or predictable; inconsistent
hook: ERRATIC: full of ERRORS, all over the place.
story: Erratic. Not regular or predictable. One hot summer in Rakib's village, the electricity followed no pattern at all. Some evenings it stayed on for hours; other days it vanished at noon, came back for ten minutes, then vanished again. Rakib kept a charged lamp beside his books, never knowing when the fan would stop. The supply was erratic. Erratic comes from the Latin for wandering, the same root as error: erratic things wander off course. So, what word describes something irregular and impossible to predict? ... Erratic.

gre.s: The athlete's performances have been so ____ this season, brilliant one week and dismal the next, that even her coaches cannot predict how she will do.
gre.clue: brilliant one week and dismal the next

example: The old office printer was maddeningly erratic, working perfectly for an hour and then jamming on every second page.

en: Thorough and complete, covering every aspect
hook: EXHAUSTIVE: covers so much it EXHAUSTS the topic.
story: Exhaustive. Thorough and complete, covering every part. Before buying a second-hand car, Raihan's father spent an entire Friday inspecting it. He checked the engine, the brakes, every tyre, the papers, and the rust under the doors, then drove it on a highway, a muddy lane and a crowded market road. Raihan counted twelve pages of notes. When his father finished, there was nothing left to check. His inspection was exhaustive. An exhaustive search exhausts every possibility. So, what word describes a check so thorough it covers every single part? ... Exhaustive.

gre.s: The committee's ____ report, which examined every expenditure over a ten-year period, left no question about where the funds had gone.
gre.clue: examined every expenditure over a ten-year period

example: Before writing her thesis on Bengali folk songs, Tahmina compiled an exhaustive list of every recording held in the national archive.

en: Possible to see coming or to predict in advance
hook: FORE-SEE-able: can be SEEN BEFORE it happens.
story: Foreseeable. Possible to see coming or to predict. A developer built a row of houses right on the bank of the Jamuna, with no embankment and no drainage. Engineers warned him; old fishermen warned him. In the very first monsoon, the river swallowed three houses. Nobody was hurt, but the owners lost everything. Everyone said the damage was foreseeable. The word is built simply: fore, meaning before, plus see, plus able. Something foreseeable is able to be seen before it happens. So, what word describes trouble that could easily have been predicted? ... Foreseeable.

gre.s: The collapse was entirely ____, since engineers had warned for years that the dam could not withstand a major flood.
gre.clue: engineers had warned for years

example: Given how little the twins had studied, their poor marks in the board exams were perfectly foreseeable.

en: Producing good or helpful results; productive
hook: FRUITFUL: a tree full of FRUIT.
story: Fruitful. Producing good or helpful results. Sadia dreaded the monthly meeting of her village women's savings group, which usually ended in arguments. This time, they agreed to buy two sewing machines, chose who would train first, and set a date to sell their clothes at the Friday haat. Walking home, Sadia [laugh] hummed all the way. The meeting had been fruitful. Picture a mango tree heavy with fruit: a fruitful effort produces plenty, while a fruitless one produces nothing. So, what word describes a meeting that produces good results? ... Fruitful.

gre.s: After decades of ____ research that yielded dozens of important discoveries, the laboratory was closed for lack of funding.
gre.clue: that yielded dozens of important discoveries

example: The partnership between the two chemists proved fruitful, producing a dozen papers and two patents within three years.

en: Of minor importance, occurring only alongside something bigger
hook: INCIDENTAL: just a side INCIDENT.
story: Incidental. Of minor importance; happening alongside something bigger. Nowshin's office sent her to Khulna for a three-day training. The training was the main purpose. Along the way she spent a little on rickshaw fares, tea and a phone card. Her manager told her to list these incidental expenses on one line at the end of her report. Next to the training, they were incidental, small costs riding along with the main trip. Think of a small incident at the side of the main road. So, what word describes a minor thing that comes along with the main one? ... Incidental.

gre.s: The lawyer argued that the photograph was merely ____ to the case, a minor detail that had no bearing on the central question of who signed the contract.
gre.clue: a minor detail that had no bearing on the central question

example: For the mountaineers, the stunning photographs were incidental, since their real goal was to measure how fast the glacier was shrinking.

en: So necessary that you cannot manage without it
hook: IN-DISPENSABLE: can NOT be dispensed with.
story: Indispensable. So necessary that you cannot manage without it. In Mehedi's joint family, Nanu is the one who knows everything: where the spare keys hang, which medicine each person takes, how much salt the dal needs, and whose birthday is next week. When she went to visit her sister in Cumilla for ten days, the house fell into chaos. Nobody could find anything. Everyone agreed she was indispensable. In means not, so indispensable means not able to be dispensed with, impossible to do without. So, what word describes someone a household simply cannot manage without? ... Indispensable.

gre.s: Once considered a luxury, reliable internet access has become ____ for students, who now need it to submit almost every assignment.
gre.clue: who now need it to submit almost every assignment

example: On long treks through the Bandarban hills, sturdy boots and plenty of drinking water are indispensable.

en: To restrain, hinder, or prevent
hook: INHIBIT: keeps you IN, holding you back.
story: Inhibit. To hold back, restrain or prevent. Tanvir knew every answer in English class, but the fear of mistakes inhibited him from speaking. Every time he tried, his throat went tight. His teacher, Nasrin Apa, started a small conversation club after school where nobody was ever marked wrong. Week by week, his voice grew steady, and one day he [laugh] cracked a joke in English. Fear had inhibited him; kindness set him free. Inhibit comes from the Latin for hold in, as if your words are held inside. So, what verb means to hold someone back from acting freely? ... Inhibit.

gre.s: Researchers hope the new compound will ____ the growth of tumors without damaging healthy tissue.
gre.clue: without damaging healthy tissue

example: Cold temperatures inhibit the growth of bacteria, which is why leftover rice should go into the fridge quickly.

en: Not giving the care or attention that duty requires
hook: NEGLIGENT: someone who NEGLECTS their duty.
story: Negligent. Failing to give the care that duty requires. For months, the tenants of an old building in Mohammadpur begged their landlord to fix a broken stair railing. He promised, collected the rent, and did nothing. Then one rainy evening, an elderly tenant slipped and broke her wrist. Her son, Kawsar, took photos of the railing to the local councillor, and the landlord was made to pay. Everyone agreed he had been negligent. A negligent person neglects their duty; the two words share a root. So, what word describes someone who fails to take proper care? ... Negligent.

gre.s: The court ruled that the landlord had been ____, since he had ignored repeated warnings about the building's faulty wiring.
gre.clue: ignored repeated warnings

example: The hospital was found negligent after a nurse gave a patient the wrong medicine despite clear labels on every bottle.

en: Completely unaware of something, often what is close by
hook: OBLIVIOUS: in OBLIVION, totally unaware.
story: Oblivious. Completely unaware of something, often what is close by. Fahim was so absorbed in his vocabulary app at Kamalapur station that he did not hear the announcement, did not notice the crowd boarding, and did not see his train to Chattogram slide away. When he finally looked up, the platform was empty. [sigh] He had learned forty words and missed his train. He had been completely oblivious. Oblivious is related to oblivion, the state of forgetting: an oblivious person has forgotten the world around them. So, what word describes someone totally unaware of what is happening nearby? ... Oblivious.

gre.s: Engrossed in her phone, the pedestrian remained completely ____ to the truck bearing down on her until a stranger grabbed her arm and pulled her back.
gre.clue: until a stranger grabbed her arm and pulled her back

example: Lost in a chess problem, Professor Haque was oblivious to the rain blowing through the open window onto his notes.

en: Done openly, where anyone can see it
hook: OVERT: right OVER the surface, out in the open.
story: Overt. Done openly, where anyone can see it. When Lubna's grandfather was young, men in his village rarely showed affection in public. But the day his granddaughter won a national science prize, he walked onto the school stage and hugged her in front of everyone, tears on his cheeks. His pride was overt, there for the whole school to see. Overt is the opposite of covert, which means hidden. Overt comes from the French word for open, so picture an open door. So, what word describes something done openly, not secretly? ... Overt.

gre.s: Though the two nations avoided ____ hostilities, never firing a shot, they waged a fierce secret war through spies and proxies.
gre.clue: they waged a fierce secret war through spies and proxies

example: The referee somehow ignored an overt shove in the penalty area, and the whole stadium erupted in boos.

en: Showing deep, sharp insight; piercing
hook: PENETRATING: goes straight through to the truth.
story: Penetrating. Showing deep, sharp insight; piercing. In his scholarship interview, Imtiaz gave a polished answer about his strengths, rehearsed many times. The interviewer, an old engineer, looked at him for a long moment and asked one quiet question: "And what did you learn from the project that failed?" It cut straight through the script. Imtiaz put down his notes and answered honestly. It was a penetrating question. To penetrate is to pierce through; a penetrating question pierces right to the truth. So, what word describes a question that cuts to the heart of a matter? ... Penetrating.

gre.s: Unlike most reviews, which merely summarized the plot, her ____ critique exposed the novel's hidden assumptions about class, insights that even the author later acknowledged.
gre.clue: Unlike most reviews, which merely summarized the plot

example: Her penetrating questions during the seminar forced the visiting economist to admit the weak points in his model.

en: Steady effort that keeps going in spite of setbacks
hook: PER-SEVERE-ANCE: persisting through SEVERE difficulty.
story: Perseverance. Steady effort that keeps going in spite of setbacks. Hasan, a farmer's son from Naogaon, failed the civil service exam on his first try. He studied for another year and failed again, by only a few marks. His friends took other jobs. Hasan bought new notebooks and sat for it a third time. When the results came, his mother [gasp] read his name twice before she believed it. He had succeeded through perseverance. Listen for severe inside it: perseverance means pushing on through severe times. So, what word names steady effort despite repeated setbacks? ... Perseverance.

gre.s: The team's eventual success owed less to brilliance than to sheer ____: they repeated the failed experiment hundreds of times before obtaining a usable result.
gre.clue: they repeated the failed experiment hundreds of times

example: Learning the sitar demands years of perseverance, since even simple melodies can take months to sound right.

en: Not genuine; fake; a person who pretends
hook: PHONY: like a fake PHONE call from a 'bank'.
story: Phony. Fake, not genuine; also, a person who pretends. At the Gabtoli bus terminal, a man in a crisp white coat sold bottles of oil he promised would cure diabetes, baldness and back pain. Framed certificates hung behind him. Shakil, a pharmacy student, looked closely and his heart sank: the seal was printed crooked, and the university did not exist. The certificates were phony, and so was the man. Phony sounds like phone, so picture a phony phone call from a fake bank asking for your password. So, what word describes something fake pretending to be real? ... Phony.

gre.s: Investigators discovered that the charity was ____: the orphanage featured in its glossy brochures did not exist, and the donations had gone straight into the founder's bank account.
gre.clue: the orphanage featured in its glossy brochures did not exist

example: The phony job agency in Motijheel collected registration fees from hundreds of graduates and then vanished overnight.

en: Devoutly religious; sometimes, falsely or showily virtuous
hook: PIOUS: PRAYING faithfully.
story: Pious. Deeply religious; sometimes, showily religious. Every dawn, Rahima Begum rises for the Fajr prayer, and every Ramadan she quietly sends rice to the families on her lane without telling anyone. Her neighbours consider her truly pious. But the word has a sharper second sense. When a businessman donates to a mosque only in front of cameras, people may call it a pious show, goodness worn for display. Pious shares a root with piety, which means devotion. So, what word describes a person deeply devoted to their faith? ... Pious.

gre.s: Voters grew weary of the senator's ____ sermons about honesty, especially once it emerged that he had lied repeatedly about his own finances.
gre.clue: once it emerged that he had lied repeatedly about his own finances

example: Her pious uncle spent the holy month in prayer and quiet study, refusing every invitation to travel or celebrate.

en: In its original, perfect condition; completely clean
hook: PRISTINE: PRIS-TEEN, as fresh and new as a teen.
story: Pristine. In its original, perfect condition; completely clean. When Rimi first visited Saint Martin's Island as a little girl, the beach was pristine: white sand, clear blue water, and not a single plastic bottle in sight. She ran into the waves shouting with joy. Twenty years later she returned with her own daughter and found wrappers drifting in the shallows. [sigh] She spent the morning picking them up. Pristine comes from the Latin for former or original: pristine means just as it was at first. So, what word describes a place untouched and perfectly clean? ... Pristine.

gre.s: Conservationists are fighting to protect one of the last ____ forests on the continent, a wilderness never touched by logging or roads.
gre.clue: never touched by logging or roads

example: The museum's copy of the first edition is still pristine, its pages crisp and white after more than two centuries.

en: Outstanding skill, especially in a particular activity
hook: PROWESS: a PRO's skill.
story: Prowess. Outstanding skill, especially in a particular activity. For two seasons, quiet Jamal sat on the bench of his village football team. Then, in the final against the neighbouring union, he came on as a substitute, dribbled past four defenders, and curled the ball into the top corner. The crowd [gasp] fell silent, then roared, and carried him home on their shoulders. Everyone talked about his prowess. Prowess sounds like pro: it is the skill of a professional, whether in sport, study or craft. So, what word means outstanding skill at something? ... Prowess.

gre.s: Despite her undoubted ____ as a chess player, she lost the championship because she could not cope with the pressure of the final game.
gre.clue: Despite her undoubted

example: The mechanic's prowess with old engines kept the village rice mill running long after spare parts had disappeared from the market.

en: To enjoy greatly; great enjoyment
bn: উপভোগ করা; তৃপ্তি সহকারে গ্রহণ করা
hook: RELISH: like a delicious RELISH sauce you savor.
story: Relish. To enjoy greatly; great enjoyment. After a year of bread and pasta in Germany, Saif came home to Dhaka. His mother set down a plate of shorshe ilish, hilsa in mustard sauce, still steaming. Saif closed his eyes at the first bite and ate slowly, savouring every mouthful. He relished it, and his mother watched with a quiet relish of her own. Relish is also a tangy sauce, like a chutney, that makes food taste better: to relish something is to taste it with joy. So, what verb means to enjoy something greatly? ... Relish.

gre.s: Far from dreading the debate, the candidate seemed to ____ the chance to confront her opponent in front of a national audience.
gre.clue: Far from dreading the debate

example: The retired judge relished long afternoons in the university library, reading the history books he never had time for while working.

en: Making false spoken statements that damage someone's reputation
hook: SLANDER is SPOKEN; LIBEL is written.
story: Slander. False spoken statements that damage someone's reputation. After losing a club election, Rony told everyone in the canteen that the winner, Fahmida, had bought votes. None of it was true, but people began to whisper when she passed. Fahmida felt her face burn in every class. Finally, the club's adviser checked the ballots, cleared her name, and made Rony apologise in front of everyone. His words had been slander. Remember: slander is spoken, while libel is written; both are false and damaging. So, what word names false spoken words that ruin a reputation? ... Slander.

gre.s: Unable to defeat his opponent on the issues, the candidate chose to ____ her instead, spreading false rumors that she had embezzled campaign funds.
gre.clue: spreading false rumors that she had embezzled campaign funds

example: Accusing a colleague of theft in front of the whole department, with no evidence at all, could expose you to a charge of slander.

en: Keeping careful watch for possible danger
hook: VIGILANT: keeping a VIGIL all night, watching.
story: Vigilant. Keeping careful watch for possible danger. During the monsoon, when the river near their village in Kurigram rises, Josna's father barely sleeps. Every few hours he walks to the embankment with a torch, checking the water against a mark on a bamboo pole, ready to wake the neighbours. One night the water climbed fast, and his warning gave everyone time to move the cattle. He was vigilant. A vigil is a night spent awake and watching; a vigilant person keeps that same watch. So, what word describes someone carefully watching for danger? ... Vigilant.

gre.s: Security guards were told to remain ____ throughout the night, since thieves had already struck the warehouse twice in the small hours.
gre.clue: since thieves had already struck the warehouse twice

example: Parents in flood-prone villages stay vigilant throughout the monsoon, keeping small children well away from the swollen river.
